sections.html:
You will find North Attleborough where Bristol County reaches its northwest corner, about 16 miles north of Providence, Rhode Island and 38 miles southwest of Boston. It covers 19.0 square miles, and 0.42 of that is water. The 2020 census counted 30,834 residents, with 12,855 households and 12,551 housing units, and the 2024 estimate is 32,135.

Plainville lies to the north, Mansfield to the east, Attleboro to the south and Cumberland, Rhode Island to the west. Villages and localities include North Attleborough Center, Attleborough Falls, Adamsdale and Sheldonville Farms. Downtown uses ZIP 02760 and Attleborough Falls uses 02763, so sellers a mile apart can have different mailing addresses.

Older mill-era streets near the center sit beside later subdivisions. An older house often comes with older wiring, an older heating system and a deed that has changed hands many times, and buyers who need a mortgage may balk at those items. That is a common reason owners of dated homes look at as-is offers.

Government here is a city manager and a nine-member council, yet residents still say Town of North Attleborough. The charter passed by vote on April 2, 2019 and started on July 1, 2019, ending the board of selectmen and a 135-seat Representative Town Meeting.

In practice, permits, inspections and municipal lien paperwork go through city departments. The city sets its own tax rate and bill dates, so call the treasurer and collector, reachable through nattleboro.com, to find out what is owed before a closing date is set.

The Ten Mile River and the Seven Mile River run through the city, along with Greenwood Lake and Falls Pond. In the north, World War I Memorial Park holds Sunrise Hill, at 390 feet the highest point in Bristol County.

Drainage is the best-known local problem, tied to a redevelopment on East Street. The former Balfour Company site at 21 East Street became a 193-unit apartment complex with 11,500 square feet of retail. Residents said it shifted drainage and flooded nearby homes. The city allowed two of three buildings to open with sixty days to address the problem.

Own a house near that area or along the rivers? Note any basement water history before you list, because an inspector will likely find it anyway. A cash buyer prices the repair rather than asking you to fix it first.

  • Older homes near the Ten Mile and Seven Mile rivers: ask about basement moisture.
  • Homes with older oil or electric heat: expect inspection questions.
  • Houses with deferred roof or heating work: a buyer's inspector will list them.

Both Interstate 95 and Interstate 295 have an exit here, and U.S. Route 1 cuts across the retail and downtown districts. State routes 120 and 152 also pass through, along with the middle stretch of Route 1A.

There is no commuter rail station inside the city. It sits about equally far from three MBTA stops in Mansfield, Attleboro Center and South Attleboro, and the Greater Attleboro Taunton Regional Transit Authority runs buses among the local towns. T.F. Green Airport in Rhode Island is about 23 miles away and Logan International is about 42 miles away.

Commuters who work in Providence or Boston are part of the buyer pool, so describe the highway access and drive times when you talk about the house. Gillette Stadium is about five miles away, and Emerald Square sits beside Allen Avenue, where one of the city's three fire stations is located.

The state sets the checklist, and it reads the same here as in any other Massachusetts community. Most sellers hire a real estate attorney, which is expected by law and by practice, and the deed is filed at the county registry of deeds as recorded land in most cases.

Start with the alarms. Before the sale, the local fire department must certify that your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet state rules. Phone the department when the closing date is set and plan for an inspection fee. The Department of Fire Services page lays out what inspectors look for.

Next comes the deed excise, set by Chapter 64D, Section 1. It is based on the price and leaves out liens that stay on the property. Your attorney will give you the exact amount at closing. One more rule, 760 CMR 74, says sellers of certain residential properties may not condition an offer on a waiver of the home inspection, so ask which rules fit your property.

sections.h2: What happens between offer and closing
sections.html:
Taking the steps in order keeps things moving. First, ask the treasurer and collector what you owe. Second, once a date is set, book the fire department. Third, give your attorney the deed, any mortgage payoff statement and notes on drainage or repairs. Fourth, the attorney arranges recording at the Bristol County registry of deeds, and the deed excise is collected at closing.

If an estate is involved or a lien remains on the property, mention it at the start. Those items add paperwork before the deed can record, and a few extra days at the beginning save a scramble at the end. Cash Home Buyers can look at the house in its present condition while these pieces are sorted out.

sections.h2: A short local history that shows in the housing
sections.html:
Settlement began in 1669 as part of Attleborough, which was incorporated in 1694. In 1887 the East Attleborough village voted to separate and took the Attleborough name, and the remainder became North Attleborough. A brass forge opened around 1780, button making followed, and jewelry became the staple trade, with Jostens and the Balfour Company both operating here in the twentieth century.

That manufacturing past explains the mix of worker housing near the center and newer subdivisions farther out. If your house is one of the older ones, collect repair receipts, permit records and any heating or roof invoices. A buyer reading a thick folder of paperwork asks fewer questions, and an investor making a cash offer can price the house faster.

The appeal of a cash sale is skipping showings, repairs and a financing contingency. A lot of owners here bought decades ago and now hold older houses whose systems would draw inspection requests.

SituationWhy a direct sale may fit
Inherited houseNo need to clear or repair before you sell
Older systemsOffer is based on the house as it is
Tenant-occupiedFewer showings to coordinate
Behind on paymentsA set closing date can be discussed

A sale here still goes through an attorney and the registry of deeds. What changes is the buyer's side of the process, and the legal steps on your side stay the same.

faqs.q: Does North Attleborough have its own property tax dates?
faqs.a: Yes. The treasurer and collector sets the tax rate and bill schedule for the city, and a phone call to that office gets you the current dates.

faqs.q: Do I need an attorney to sell a house in North Attleborough?
faqs.a: Practically speaking, yes. Real estate attorneys are a normal part of Massachusetts sales, and the closing ends with the deed being recorded at the registry of deeds.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate to sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The local fire department must certify that your alarms meet sale requirements. Book the visit once a closing date is set, and expect to pay a fee.

faqs.q: Is North Attleborough a town or a city?
faqs.a: Both names show up. The 2019 charter created a city government with a manager and nine councilors, but the community kept calling itself the Town of North Attleborough.
Bristol County, at its registry of deeds. Your attorney files the deed and pays the excise when it records.
